problem: Existing QA datasets fail to train systems to perform complex reasoning and provide explanations for answers.
method: Introduces HotpotQA, a dataset with 113k Wikipedia-based QA pairs featuring: (1) questions requiring reasoning over multiple supporting documents; (2) diverse questions not tied to predefined KBs/schemas; (3) sentence-level supporting facts for strong supervision and explainability; (4) factoid comparison questions to test fact extraction and comparison.
key_assumptions: Providing sentence-level supporting facts enables models to learn multi-hop reasoning and explain predictions.
main_contribution: HotpotQA dataset for diverse, explainable multi-hop question answering, showing it is challenging for latest QA systems and that supporting facts improve performance and explainability.
results: ["HotpotQA is challenging for latest QA systems; supporting facts enable models to improve performance and make explainable predictions."]

relation_to_idea.conceptual_difference: HotpotQA provides a benchmark dataset for multi-hop reasoning with supporting facts, whereas the idea focuses on training LMs with enriched context subgraphs, adaptive repair loops, and RL transfer to improve multi-hop KGQA performance.
